notes: Module is pure — no GenServer, no Agent, no Process.put/get, no module-level state.
try/rescue wrapping Lua.RuntimeException and Lua.CompilerException is correct and idiomatic for C-binding exceptions from a NIF-backed library.
Function guard 'when is_binary(script_source)' adds a light compile-time narrowing — appropriate.
Return shapes are {:ok, %{manifest_hash: ...}} | {:error, term()} consistently with the behaviour contract.
Executor starts no processes. Lua.t() is a plain value allocated and discarded within a single function call.
No supervision tree changes. No unsupervised spawn.
Diff is exactly the expected surface: lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex, test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs, lib/letflow/design/req153-lua-executor.md, and handoff files.
lua_script_audit.ex is NOT in the diff — isolation invariant preserved.
No resource limits, no capability enforcement, no manifest validation added — all correctly deferred to REQ-154–REQ-158 per design doc §8.
Sandbox.new/0 is used as the sole construction path — matches REQ-151/152 design and INV-SBX-1.
Moduledoc states the concrete script_ref shape: 'a binary containing the Lua source text to execute'. AC7 covered.

FINDING (non-blocking): @moduledoc does not cite docs/migration/decisions/0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md. The module references REQ-153 and LUA-02 correctly, but the decision record that chose Lua as the scripting runtime is not cross-referenced. This is a documentation gap, not a correctness defect — the implementation is fully consistent with that decision.
script_ref is typed as binary() and guarded at the function head. No representable-as-invalid-state gap observed at this scope.
8 acceptance criteria covered. async: true is safe — no DB access; INV-LSA-1/LSA-2 paths short-circuit before any Repo insert.
AC3/AC4 verify isolation at the Sandbox.new() level directly — reasonable given that execute_with_manifest/2 delegates construction to Sandbox.new/0; property is proven at the right layer.
Syntax error test (bonus) uses '===' which is not valid Lua syntax and will reliably trigger CompilerException — correct choice.
